title: a function that both throws a recoverable Error and calls panic(...) publishes only the recoverable Error in its inferred row
notes: specification/failures.mdx §Panic Does Not Widen a Return Type: 'Calling `panic(...)` MUST NOT force a function's return type to widen into `Result<A, Panic>`.' and 'A function that validates an argument, refuses a forgery, or asserts an invariant MUST therefore be able to abort with `panic(...)` while keeping a plain return type.' docs/DECISIONS.md carries the matching Locked entry ('Calling `panic(...)` does not widen a return type into `Result<A, Panic>` … the prohibition is on the compiler forcing it'). `E` is the expected-error channel (reference/function-channels.mdx) and a panic is not an expected error, so a construct that aborts with `panic(...)` keeps whatever return type it declares. THE FAIL-OPEN GATE. This is the shape that must not regress when the non-widening rule is implemented, and it is the one place where closing the reported rule carelessly would have made the language LESS sound rather than more. specification/failures.mdx: 'The distinguished panic case is tracked separately from ordinary recoverable Error variants' and 'Ordinary Result recovery MUST NOT swallow panic implicitly.' `force` genuinely has a Result channel here — it throws `Missing` — so an implementation that decides whether to materialize a panic by asking 'does this function return some Result?' answers yes and turns the panic into the error variant of Result<string, Missing>. That is what line 3 measures: before the rule landed this program compiled with ZERO diagnostics, published the row ["Missing","Panic"], emitted __vsResultFailure(__vsPanicValue(...)) for the panic, and printed "missing: empty key" — an invariant violation arriving in the caller's expected-error branch wearing the name of a lookup miss. The materialization decision must key on the PUBLISHED ROW naming Panic, not on the presence of any Result. Lines 1 and 2 are the over-correction guard on the same program: an implementation that stopped materializing panics by dropping the whole failure row would break them. 09-foreign-calls/explicit-panic-charges-the-channel is the third corner — the row that DOES name Panic, where materialization is required.
